Gate: ① — a product defect with a named landing point: published skill text that says a wrong sentence (North Star priority item 4 — a sentence a skill gets wrong is a product defect). **reach:** a named real producer — `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md` ships to every project through `npx skills add` (the Studio author's skill). Its Routing model section, line 375 on `origin/main` `fbcbcf124f`, reads: "There is no dedicated `doc` nav-item type yet, so use a `url` item pointing at `/docs/…`"; and `skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json` eval 4's `expected_output` expects "a `type: 'url'` nav item pointing at `/docs/crm_user_guide`". The contract: `packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts:108` declares `'doc'` among the navigation-item types, with the two shapes documented at lines 681–686 (`{ type: 'doc', book }` opens the book as its first readable page with the book sidebar; `{ type: 'doc', doc }` opens that page), and `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md` line 176 already lists `doc` in its Navigation Item Types table ("`book?` / `doc?` (one required), `label`, `icon` — Package docs; inherits docs audience"). So the entry file teaches the type and the rules file tells the author it does not exist; an author following `pages.md` writes a `url` item where the platform has a typed one, and the eval pins the wrong answer.

**Expected.** `pages.md` Routing model teaches the `doc` item (the book and doc shapes; when a `url` item is still right, e.g. an anchor into a page), and eval 4 expects it.
